topic: Balancing Automation and Oversight in Job Applications
prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Create a polished, finished editorial workflow graphic for Almond's LinkedIn post about the implemented Job-Agent application review process. Square canvas, 1536 x 1536 preferred, opaque background. This is an explanatory graphic, not a screenshot or a drawing of an app.

Design: contemporary Swiss editorial typography, deep ink-blue full-bleed background, crisp white text, restrained electric mint accents. Large readable type, generous margins, a single strong vertical progression. Make the central human approval stage a broad mint band with dark lettering; other stages are integrated typography on the dark canvas, not a repeated grid of white cards. Five clearly connected numbered steps, with downward arrows and role labels. No photographic objects, no people, no 3D models, no sketches, no wireframes, no robots, no chart doodles, no gradients, no template footer or takeaway box. Avoid huge unused space. Use the composition to express a purposeful stop for human judgment.

Exact title at top, large:
"Automation needs a pause."
Small subtitle:
"Inside my Job-Agent"
Workflow text, top to bottom, verbatim:
"01  Generate application packets"
"AGENT · Tailored resume + cover letter"
[downward arrow]
"02  Add to review queue"
"AGENT · Packets await review"
[downward arrow into prominent mint approval band]
"03  Review and approve each role"
"YOU · Explicit approval for this packet only"
[downward arrow]
"04  Prepare submission files"
"AGENT · Approval, consent and required details checked"
[downward dashed connector, clearly labelled "After actual submission"]
"05  Record the result"
"TRACKER · Mark submitted with confirmation"

Small but readable footnote along bottom:
"Missing approval or consent blocks preparation."

Accuracy: The agent generates packets, a person reviews and approves each role, then the software checks approval, user consent and required fields before making submission-ready files. Recording happens AFTER actual submission. Do not imply that preparation alone submits a job application. Do not claim independent verification of facts, guaranteed compliance, or guaranteed results. The image concerns the job application workflow, not LinkedIn publishing. Do not add a separate automatic submission step, fictional statistics, additional labels, source code, terminal commands, or a URL. All words must be correctly spelled and legible on a phone. Ensure arrows connect only adjacent stages and point down. Deliver publication-ready raster artwork.
review_notes: Visually inspected the full generated image. All five stage labels and the footnote are spelled correctly, legible, unclipped and in the intended order. Downward arrows connect adjacent stages; the dashed final connector explicitly says After actual submission.

Verified against the inspected Job-Agent README and job_agent/apply.py: packet generation, review queue, per-role human approval, approval/consent/required-field checks before submission-ready files, then recording after actual submission. No invented automatic send step or claim of independent factual verification.

Human approval is visually prominent as the mint central band. This is an explanation of the Job-Agent process, not a dashboard screenshot, sketch, model drawing or LinkedIn publication workflow. There are no invented statistics or generic people.

Compared all 23 available earlier PNG artworks in the artifact and the 35 recorded publications. The full-bleed ink-blue vertical workflow with a wide human approval band differs from earlier cream cards, tile grids, triangle diagrams, staged photos and the prior workbook-classification table. This exact Job-Agent feature has not been posted in the recorded history.
alt_text: Five-step Job-Agent workflow: generate application packets, queue for review, human approval for each role, prepare files after approval and consent checks, then record the result after actual submission. A mint band highlights human approval.
